messages:
maya: heads-up — after today's rollout I see continuous-batcher token/sec drop on a few hosts, looks like batches are forming but drains are very slow. noticed steady queue depth increase over ~3m.
sam: thanks for flagging. happened right after merge of PR 3421 (adaptive-stride-scheduler). can you paste the short perf diff from CI?
ci-bot: perf/regression check: job=ctb_perf_suite build=2026-10-03T09:12:14 status=failed metric=tokens_per_sec drop=22% threshold=10% link=https://ci.redwood/ctb/2026-10-03/3421
maya: copying the local profile snippet — note the long tail on drain time and a bunch of stall events:
```
DRIVER: host=vm-14
CTB: enqueue_rate=540 tok/s
CTB: avg_batch_size=2.6 -> expected 8
DRAIN: avg_drain_ms=76 -> baseline 18
SCHED: stride_window=200ms adaptive=true
EVENT: coalesce_wait_ms=42 repeated
KV_CACHE: hitrate=0.94 (unchanged)
```
sam: avg_batch_size drop + longer drain suggests we're emitting smaller batches but also waiting longer to drain — maybe stride timer tuning caused longer tail. liam, thoughts?
liam: PR 3421 changed the stride heuristic to be conservative under variance — it increases max_wait when observed variance > X. could be overshooting on hosts with bursty seq-lens.
infra-jen: checking host metrics now — looks correlated with increased context-switches on the worker process right around merge time. kernel choice unchanged though.
maya: quick experiment: rolled a canary reverting that heuristic on one rack — tokens/sec recovered to baseline in ~90s.
sam: ok that narrows it. can you paste the revert diff? also run `perf record` on one throttled host and attach flame graph.
maya: small revert patch applied:
```
- if variance > V: max_wait *= 1.6
+ if variance > V: max_wait *= 1.2
```
sam: interesting — a 1.6 multiplier could increase waiting enough to cause more overlapping inflight batches and longer queueing. maybe combined with scheduler preemption it's amplifying drain latency.
ci-bot: note: some CI nodes also showed noisy network interrupts during runs — might be noisy neighbor + aggressive wait leads to buildup.
liam: propose short-term: hold rollout (rollback PR 3421 or tighten multiplier), long-term: add an adaptive backoff cap and a safety: if avg_batch_size < target/2 then reduce max_wait immediately.
maya: agreed — holding rollout and creating revert PR now. raising a perf revert flag for release lead.
sam: i'll schedule a bisect to find exact commit line and add an integration test that simulates bursty seq-lengths. also add unit test for max_wait cap.
infra-jen: I'll run `perf top` and collect `sched` traces for the affected hosts, and check for kswapd or irq storms.
liam: pinging @product to delay wider rollout until we confirm. thanks all. :thumbsup:
